message.content: Without using any tools, explain in three sentences what `git rebase --onto` does.

content.text: `git rebase --onto <newbase> <upstream> <branch>` takes the commits on `<branch>` that come after `<upstream>` and replays them on top of `<newbase>`. That lets you move a range of commits to a completely different base, not just to the tip of the branch they came from. For example, `git rebase --onto main featureA featureB` moves only the commits unique to `featureB` (the ones not in `featureA`) onto `main`. You can also use it to cut commits out of a branch, as in `git rebase --onto HEAD~3 HEAD~1`, which drops the two commits before the current one.
